tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Classical global Dirichlet solvability] 1. ch6:6.14\group gt-ch06 Under Theorem 6.13, if $\Omega $ is $C^{2,\alpha }$ and $f$, the coefficients, and $\varphi $ are respectively in $C^\alpha (\bar\Omega )$, $C^\alpha (\bar\Omega )$, and $C^{2,\alpha }(\bar\Omega )$, then the unique solution belongs to $C^{2,\alpha }(\bar\Omega )$.
Proof

\sketch Apply Theorem 6.13, straighten the boundary near each point, and use Lemma 6.10 and the local boundary estimate to identify the solution with the local $C^{2,\alpha }$ Dirichlet solution.

□
